What is the cause of Periodicity of elements in the periodic table? How do the following properties vary in a group? i. Atomic size ii. Ionization energy In the Modern periodic table all the elements are arranged according to the increasing order of atomic number and the elements having similar properties are repeated after regular intervals.
This phenomenon is known as periodicity and the properties are known as periodic properties.
Variation of atomic size in a group of periodic table: i.
Ionization energy decreases with increase in atomic size because the larger the distance from the nucleus, the lesser will be the attraction between the nucleus and the valence electrons.
Larger the size of atom, lesser the value of Electron affinity.
Variation of ionization energy in a group of periodic table: ii.
When we move from top to bottom, the I.E. gradually decreases. This is due to increase in atomic size.
Increase in number of inner electrons which brings the increase in shielding effect on the outermost electron.
Increase in nuclear charge from top to bottom in a group whose effect is less than the effect of increasing åtomic size and shielding effect.
